correctness.rationale: In dimension two, componentwise inversion agrees projectively with the swap J, since (1/x,1/y)=(y,x)/(xy). Write D_r=diag(r,1−r), D_s=diag(s,1−s). The exact full sweep is projectively the action of T=D_s J KᵀD_r J K. Apart from its left diagonal multiplier, T has entries α=rbc+(1−r)ad, β=bd, γ=ac, δ=rad+(1−r)bc. In x=v_1/v_2, the map is a positive constant times (αx+β)/(γx+δ). Its log-coordinate derivative is (αδ−βγ)/[αγx+αδ+βγ+βδ/x], with nonnegative numerator r(1−r)(ad−bc)². Minimizing the denominator by AM–GM gives (√(αδ)+√(βγ))² at x=√(βδ/(αγ)); derivative sharpness is global by the mean-value theorem and arbitrarily close inputs at the peak. Since αδ/(βγ)=1+r(1−r)(R−1)²/R, this is the claimed q. For R=1 the map is constant; otherwise q<1 and Banach's theorem on the whole real log-ratio line gives the stated convergence bound. The factor increases strictly with r(1−r) for R≠1 and at r=1/2 reduces to the stated classical kernel-only bound. Transposition and exchange of the marginals give the reverse-order comparison, not a trajectory-wise or local rate claim. The example rounds to the displayed values. The package numerical check was inspected but not run; it does not certify the all-input claim.
